Unwanted Christmas presents result in a massive waste of people's time and money and an enormous amount of landfill. It's time to encourage each other to give to charity instead.

Insight: We need reciprocal permission not to give each other gifts to avoid disappointment or embarrassment.

The Christmas Treaty helps two people agree not to buy each other Christmas presents. Instead, each donates what they would have spent to a charity chosen by the other.

Personalised Treaty page: Display the two participants, agreed amounts, charity choices and current status.
Choose a charity: Select from a curated list of 20 charities, with links to their official donation pages.

Keep the first version simple.

No payment processing or money collection.

Track key steps in the user journey.

We are looking for a developer who can think strategically, structure the system cleanly, and build something that is reliable, extensible, and launch-ready.
Project Overview
We are building a pre-launch waitlist experience for a fintech product. The system should allow users to join early, complete their profile, refer friends, earn rewards, and later transition into the main app once it launches.
This backend will power the full waitlist and referral journey.
Project Scope
We need a backend system that supports the following user flow and business logic:
1. Waitlist Signup
A user joins the waitlist by entering their email address.
Once this happens, the system should:
- create a new user record
- prevent duplicate registrations
- assign 100 Coins
- generate a unique referral code / referral link
- trigger an automated welcome email
- include a personalized dashboard link in that email
2. Profile Completion Reward
After signup, the user may complete their profile by entering:
- full name
- phone number
Once both fields are successfully submitted and saved, the system should:
- update the user record
- award an additional 400 Coins
- ensure this bonus is only granted once
- update the user’s dashboard / reward totals
3. Referral Reward System
Each user should have a unique referral link.
When a referred user signs up through that link, the system should track the referral and award the referring user:
- 500 Coins per referral
- $20 cash per referral
The backend must keep a clear record of:
- who referred whom
- which referrals converted
- how many coins were earned from referrals
- how much cash was earned from referrals
- referral status and timestamps
We want the logic to be designed carefully so the system can avoid duplicate credits, self-referrals, or inaccurate tracking wherever possible.
4. Coin Milestones / Reward Logic
The coin system should support the following reward milestones:
- 2,500 coins = 2 months free premium membership
- 3,000 coins = 3 months free premium membership
The backend should track each user’s total coin balance and progression toward these milestone rewards.
5. Automated Welcome Email
After initial signup, the system should automatically send a welcome email that includes:
- confirmation that the user joined the waitlist
- their personalized dashboard link
- an overview of how rewards work
- information on how to earn more coins and cash
Please recommend the email service/provider you would use and explain why.

THE PROBLEM
Churn takes back about 4–5% of MRR every month. A third of this month's churn is failed payments, and our recovery flows broke twice this year before anyone noticed. We already have the data and the agents. What's missing is one person who owns the number and runs the loop every day.

WHAT'S ALREADY BUILT (you don't start from zero)
- An internal agentic CRM. It puts billing, product usage, support and call data on one card per customer, and it has an MCP server you can query from Claude Code.
- Hourly at-risk lists with the money at stake: cancellation booked, payment failed, WhatsApp disconnected, stopped using the app.
- A churn agent that looks into each account, gives a verdict and drafts a letter. A second agent fact-checks the letter, and a person decides whether to send it.
- A 10% control group that never gets contacted, so every action is measured against doing nothing.
- All rules live in GitHub. You change a rule through a pull request.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN
1. Failed payments, first. Make sure every failed invoice reaches the recovery flow (Stripe + Churnkey), and check every week that the campaigns are actually firing. Build a same-day track for bigger accounts across email, SMS, in-app chat and WhatsApp.
2. Booked cancellations. Every one gets a decision within 24 hours, and you reach out to the ones worth saving.

4. Win-back and reconnect. Bring back customers who left, plus customers who still pay but whose WhatsApp went dark.
5. Better agents. When a letter is wrong, fix the rule behind it (prompt, template or threshold), not just that one letter. The aim is to safely move small accounts to automatic sending.
6. Root causes. Each month, report the top 3 churn reasons in dollars to the product team, with customer quotes.
7. A weekly written update with your numbers.

TARGETS FOR YOUR FIRST 3 MONTHS
- Churned MRR down about 20%
- Failed-payment recovery back to at least 77% (our 2025 level) and above the control group
- 100% of booked cancellations decided within 24 hours
- Every at-risk account paying $300+/month has a named person within 1 working day

YOU'LL FIT IF YOU
- Run AI workflows yourself every day (Claude Code or Codex, MCP, agents, n8n/Make, scripts) and can show us real examples.
- Have owned retention, churn or customer success in B2B SaaS, ideally self-serve with SMB customers, and know your numbers: churned MRR, recovery rate, save rate.

Home service companies lose jobs because they answer new leads hours later, or never. A homeowner with a broken AC or a leaking roof calls the first company that responds. 5. Hand off to a human immediately for emergencies, upset customers, or anything out of scope.

7. Follow up automatically if the lead goes quiet (e.g., 5 min, 2 hrs, next day, day 3) and stop the moment they reply.

- Claude API for the conversation and lead scoring

- Error handling and alerts if any step fails. Leads can never silently disappear.

STACK

DELIVERABLES
- Working workflows in my accounts (I own everything)
- Exported workflow JSON + prompt files
- Written documentation + Loom walkthrough
- A setup checklist so the system can be deployed for a new company in a few hours

BUDGET & TIMELINE

leads.title: transcription of 32 English-language call recordings (309 minutes) - fixed price, fast turnaround
leads.desc:
Overview

I need accurate, human verbatim transcripts of 32 recorded telephone calls between a customer and a UK equine insurance company’s claims team. Total audio is 5 hours 9 minutes (309 minutes). Files are MP4 (audio only).. All speakers are native English speakers (UK accents). I want a fixed price for the whole job and a fast turnaround - please state your price and delivery time in your proposal.

Accuracy is essential. These transcripts may be used in legal proceedings, so every word matters. This must be a human listening exercise. Automated/AI transcription on its own is not acceptable. If you use software as a first pass, you must then listen to every file in full and correct it line by line. I will spot-check transcripts against the audio.

Format - one document per recording (Word or plain text), same filename as the audio file. At the top of each transcript:

- Date: DD/MM/YY. Take this from the filename, which begins with the date in DDMMYY format (e.g. 110226 - Holly Williams (1519 UTC).mp4 is 11/02/26).
- Time of call: copy the time exactly as shown in the filename, e.g. “15:19 UTC”. Do not convert it. If the filename has no time, write “Time: not stated in filename”.
- Length of recording: total duration in minutes and seconds.
- Parties: the filename gives the insurer’s call handler by name. Identify the other party (and any further people who join) from the content of the call. List everyone who speaks.

In the body of the transcript:

- Verbatim, speaker-labelled by name (e.g. “Holly Williams:” / “Alex Maclean:”). Where a speaker’s name is not given, label them by role (e.g. “NFU Mutual - receptionist”) and switch to the name once it is known.
- Where a call is transferred or another person joins, mark it clearly (e.g. “[Call transferred - new speaker: Ella Fazakerley, claims handler]”) and continue labelling the new speaker correctly.
- Note every hold or pause of more than about 10 seconds with its length, e.g. “[On hold - 2 min 40 sec]” or “[Pause - 15 sec]”.
- Add a timestamp [mm:ss] at least every two minutes and at every speaker change after a hold or transfer.
- Mark anything you cannot make out as “[inaudible 00:00]” with the timestamp rather than guessing. Flag any term you don’t understand or aren’t sure you’ve heard correctly by writing it as best you can and adding “[?]” after it, e.g. “proximal suspensory desmitis [?]” or “Arthramid [?]”. leads.title: Minimal vector line art
leads.desc:
I’m looking for a skilled line-art illustrator to create clean, minimal drawings from reference photos, mainly animals and pets.

This is not standard vector tracing. The goal is to simplify each photograph while keeping the specific subject recognizable and accurate.

What I need:

Preserve the subject’s actual pose, silhouette and proportions
Preserve important facial features and distinctive characteristics
Use as few lines as possible
Remove the entire background
Remove shadows, texture and unnecessary details
Remove most fur/hair detail
Do not cartoonize, beautify or redesign the subject
Do not add details that are not visible in the photo
Keep the remaining lines faithful to the original photo

A simple way to describe the goal is:

Simplify by removing information, not by redesigning the subject.

I am especially interested in illustrators with strong observational drawing skills who can decide which lines are essential for recognition and which can be removed.

Project:
We will start with a small paid test (1–2 images). If the results are a good fit, the first project will likely be around 10–20 illustrations, with potential for a larger ongoing project.

Preferred deliverables:

AI or SVG vector file preferred
High-resolution PNG
Clean dark linework on a white background

High-quality raster illustration (for example Procreate) may also be considered if the illustration quality is excellent.

Please apply with examples of line drawings created from photographs, especially animals, portraits, or other organic subjects. If possible, please show both the original photo and your resulting drawing.

Important: The commissioned artwork is intended to be used as training data for an AI model being developed for a commercial product. Applicants must be comfortable granting the necessary commercial and AI-training usage rights.

leads.title: AI Agent Development
leads.desc:
We're looking for a developer to build an AI agent that handles first-line customer support – answering common questions, pulling order and account information, and escalating to a human when it can't resolve something.

A bit about us: we're a B2C e-commerce company handling around 3,000 support tickets a month, currently all answered manually by a small team.

What we want the agent to do:
– Answer customer questions from our own knowledge base and documentation, not from general knowledge – responses should be grounded in our content, with sources it can point to.
– Pull live data (order status, account details, shipping) from our systems via API, and act on it within the conversation.
– Know its limits: recognise when it can't help and hand off cleanly to a human agent, passing along the full context.
– Stay in scope: politely decline questions outside its remit, and never invent answers when it's unsure.

– Accuracy and safety: minimal hallucination, sensible guardrails, and predictable behaviour on edge cases.

– Scalability and cost control: the design should handle growing volume without runaway token costs.
– Data privacy: customer data handled in line with GDPR.

Scope and context:
– Systems to connect to: our order management system and customer accounts, both of which expose REST APIs; our help desk (Zendesk) for ticket creation and human handoff.
– Where our knowledge lives now: a mix of our public help centre and internal support docs in Notion.
– Expected volume: around 3,000 conversations a month to start, with seasonal peaks roughly double that.
– Model/platform: open to your recommendation, though we'd lean toward a well-supported, production-proven provider.

– How you'd approach the build, and the overall architecture

– How you'd manage ongoing costs

Checks the communication dashboard for queued messages.

Never sends emails or faxes or presses communication send buttons.

We're building a company of AI characters.
Each of our characters is a brand with a personality: their own story, their own voice and their own world. We grow them with paid video ads on Meta, and every day tens of thousands of people discover them through the creative we make.

Ads are the engine of this company. Every character grows or stalls on its creative. We're looking for the person who owns that engine: the scripts, the hooks, the scenes, and the call on what we test next.

Every week you sit down with our media buyer and look at the truth: which hooks stopped the scroll, which ads made money and which ones died. Then you decide what we test next.

You write the voice-over scripts, and they sound like a real person talking, not like an ad. If a line reads well but sounds fake out loud, it isn't done yet.

You come up with the hooks and the scenes, and you make them in our own AI studio. Image, video and voice generation are already built in, so you spend your time on ideas, not on fighting tools.

You cut the final ads in CapCut (or whatever you're fastest in): captions, pacing, versions to test.

Who we're looking for
You've made direct-response ads that worked, and you can show us the numbers. Hook rate, CTR, CPA: you know what they mean and what moves them.
Your English is excellent, and you have an ear for how real people talk.
You've generated AI images and video yourself, and it bothers you when something looks fake.
You can edit. Not like a pro colorist, but fast and with good instincts.
You don't wait to be told. You see a pattern in the data and you've already got three tests ready.
You'd rather ship ten good ads than one perfect one.
You can hear "this one flopped" and think "interesting" instead of "ouch".

Who this is not for
Brand people who've never looked at a cost-per-result.
Anyone without real DTC / performance marketing experience.
Anyone who hasn't actually generated AI images or video themselves.
Anyone who needs a detailed brief for every task.
Anyone who freezes when things move fast. We test a lot, deadlines are real, and some weeks are intense.

The deal
Long-term, remote, about 15 hours a week to start, and more as we grow.
You work directly with our founder and our media buyer. No layers, no agency politics.
We pay for results. If you're great at this, you'll grow with the company.
At least 3 hours a day overlapping with Prague time (CET).

you apply → a short paid test (2–3 hours) → a paid trial week → we build this together.

Project Overview

We are an established international athletic development company looking for an experienced Computer Vision / Machine Vision Engineer to help develop a proprietary camera-based athlete testing and performance analysis system.

Our objective is to develop reliable technology that uses video footage to accurately measure athletic performance without relying on traditional electronic timing gates or wireless sensors.

We're looking for an engineer with strong experience in OpenCV, video processing, object tracking, camera calibration, and accurate physical measurements using cameras.

Phase 1 – Camera-Based Athlete Testing

leads.title: Build Internal Client Onboarding Platform — Google Cloud, Next.js, Claude API
leads.desc:
I run a CPA firm and we onboard roughly five new clients a week. Right now that process is held together by a Calendly booking, an optional intake form, an Excel tracker, a Dropbox folder, and a lot of manual email. My team spends more time moving information between those systems than they do on actual client work, and things fall through the cracks — mostly prospects who book a meeting without filling out the intake form, and clients who stall mid-onboarding without anyone noticing.

I want to replace that with a single internal web app that my firm logs into with our Google Workspace accounts.

What it needs to do:

A Calendly webhook creates the client record. The app matches the optional intake form to that record by email and flags anyone who booked without submitting one. It generates a research brief and a draft pre-meeting email for my staff to review and edit — drafts get written into Gmail, and a person sends them. Nothing goes to a client automatically. After the meeting, one button creates the document folder and sends the tax organizer. As documents come in, the app checks them against the expected list and tells me what's missing. When I approve, it triggers the DocuSign engagement letter and updates the client's status. Discounts and scope changes need to be real states in the pipeline, not exceptions that drop off the board.

Stack I have in mind (open to being argued out of any of it):

Google Cloud — Cloud Run, Cloud SQL, Secret Manager, Document AI. Next.js front end behind Google Workspace SSO. Calendly and DocuSign APIs. Claude API for the drafting and research work.

Important: we handle tax documents, so this falls under the FTC Safeguards Rule and IRS Pub 4557. I need someone who takes that seriously — SSO and MFA through Workspace, encryption at rest and in transit, an append-only audit log of every automated action and human approval, and a short write-up of the architecture I can attach to our written information security plan.

Looking for: someone comfortable across backend, front end, and cloud infrastructure who can scope this into phases and ship the first one. Python or TypeScript both fine. Prior work with GCP and with LLM APIs in a production setting matters more to me than a specific framework.

Happy to discuss budget and timeline. I'd like to start with a paid discovery phase — map the current process, agree on the data model, and come back with a phased plan before writing much code.

leads.title: Odoo ERP Developer & AI Automation Specialist | Odoo 19, AI Agents, API Integrations
leads.desc:
We are looking for an experienced Odoo ERP Developer, Odoo Technical Consultant, and AI Automation Specialist to help us implement, customize, integrate, and automate business processes using Odoo ERP and modern AI technologies.

The ideal candidate has hands-on experience with Odoo ERP implementation, Odoo customization, Python development, AI automation, workflow automation, API integration, and business process optimization. You should be comfortable building scalable ERP solutions, integrating AI tools, automating repetitive tasks, and developing custom Odoo modules tailored to business requirements.

Experience with Odoo 16, Odoo 17, Odoo 18, and Odoo 19 is preferred.

Key Responsibilities

Implement, configure, customize, and optimize Odoo ERP solutions.

Develop custom Odoo modules using Python, PostgreSQL, XML, JavaScript, and OWL.

Customize Odoo CRM, Sales, Purchase, Inventory, Accounting, Invoicing, Manufacturing, HR, and eCommerce modules.

Build AI-powered workflows, intelligent automation, and AI agents integrated with Odoo ERP.

Integrate OpenAI, ChatGPT, Claude AI, LLMs, and other AI APIs with Odoo.

Develop AI chatbots, automated customer support, lead qualification, lead scoring, and intelligent CRM automation.

Automate business processes, data entry, invoice processing, document extraction, reporting, and repetitive administrative tasks.

Integrate Odoo with third-party applications, REST APIs, webhooks, payment gateways, accounting platforms, and external databases.

Develop custom REST API endpoints and synchronize data between Odoo and external systems.

Build workflow automation using n8n, Make, Zapier, and Python scripts where appropriate.

Implement AI-powered OCR, document processing, invoice recognition, and intelligent data extraction.

Configure automated notifications, approval workflows, scheduled actions, and server actions.

Perform Odoo migration, version upgrades, data migration, performance optimization, debugging, and troubleshooting.

Work with Odoo Online, Odoo.sh, and self-hosted Odoo deployments.

Improve ERP efficiency through AI integration, process automation, and scalable technical solutions.

Required Skills

Odoo 19, Odoo 18, Odoo 17, Odoo 16

REST API, Webhooks, JSON

AI Automation and Intelligent Workflows

OpenAI API, ChatGPT API, Claude API

Generative AI and Business Process Automation

leads.title: Web Designer Needed for Premium Website Redesign
leads.desc:
We are looking for an experienced freelance web designer to redesign our website: chi-cafe.de.

The goal is to create a modern, premium, and visually appealing website with a strong focus on:

- Excellent typography
- Beautiful imagery
- Clean and elegant layouts
- A calm, high-quality visual experience
- Strong mobile responsiveness
- A design that feels modern, trustworthy, and polished

As a design reference, we like the look and feel of websites such as ouraring.com — especially the clean structure, strong use of typography, premium visual language, and image-led storytelling.

Scope of work
We are looking for someone who can help with:

- Website redesign concept
- Homepage design
- Visual direction and design system
- Typography, colors, spacing, and image usage
- Mobile and desktop designs
- Optional: support with implementation, depending on your skills

Ideal candidate
You should have:

- Strong experience in modern web design
-A good eye for typography and visual hierarchy
- Experience designing premium consumer-facing websites
- A portfolio with clean, elegant, image-driven websites
Ability to create designs that are beautiful but also practical to implement

Please include examples of relevant website design work in your application.

We are looking for a designer who can bring a fresh, high-quality visual direction to the website while keeping the user experience clear and intuitive.

leads.title: Data Analysis AI Agent
leads.desc:

- Analyze inventory balance, monthly sales reports, backorder reports and customer orders/projections to determine Inventory coverage for 4-6 months stock holdings 
- Flag out short expiry and excessive stocks for commercial team to promote sales 
- Suggest potential stock shifts from Main warehouses to maintain healthy coverage and/or fulfill urgent requirements and internal consignment shifts
- Draft out stock shift picking slips using existing excel templates based on planned inventory  

 
Sales and procurement analysis and preparation 

- Upload data from external parties into the working file 
- Analyze and develop a forecast inventory consumption using past month sales trends, potential projections and new customers onboarding initial loading 
- Prepare replenishment quantities for each product to ensure healthy inventory coverage 
- Draft Purchase order forms using existing excel templates and replenishment quantity based on inventory planning 
- Suggest and highlight discrepancies and difference compared to initial orders at the end of production cycle

leads.title: Shopify CRO Specialist Needed to Optimize Clothing Product Pages & Boost Conversions
leads.desc:
We're looking for a Shopify expert with strong Conversion Rate Optimization (CRO) experience to improve our dropshipping clothing product pages and turn more visitors into buyers.

The goal isn't just to make the pages look better. We want a smoother shopping experience, stronger product presentation, and fewer reasons for customers to leave without purchasing.

What You'll Work On:

Optimize existing Shopify product pages for better conversions.

Improve product descriptions, titles, images, and product layouts.

Review product page structure, pricing presentation, and trust elements.

Identify friction points that may be causing visitors to abandon their purchases.

Improve mobile responsiveness and the overall shopping experience.

Recommend CRO improvements for product page buttons, size guides, shipping information, and customer reviews.

Ensure the pages look clean, professional, and consistent with our clothing brand.

What We're Looking For:

Hands-on experience with Shopify stores, preferably clothing or fashion brands.

A solid understanding of CRO principles and e-commerce customer behavior.

Experience improving product page layouts and user experience.

The ability to explain what needs improvement and why.

A results-focused approach rather than unnecessary redesigns.

To Apply:

Please share examples of Shopify product pages you've optimized and briefly explain what changes you made to improve the customer experience or conversion potential.

We're looking for someone who can identify the real issues, suggest practical improvements, and implement them effectively.

Élan helps local businesses in Luxembourg and the German border region grow online. We’re AI-first: the engine that finds, captures and follows up on new customers runs on automation, so a small business never misses an opportunity. The name means momentum — forward drive, speed. We’ve done the strategy. We need someone to turn it into an identity that looks like nothing else in this market.

The core idea: momentum as a timeline
We don’t sell a pile of disconnected services. A client moves forward along a timeline, and services hang off that line. The brand has to express that forward motion — a system building speed, from standstill to full acceleration.

How Élan works — the four stages (this is the backbone of the symbol set)

Foundation — a website and brand built to convert, not just to look nice. The site is the funnel everything attaches to. The first push from standstill.
Visibility — getting found by the right local people: Google Business Profile, local SEO, reputation. Picking up speed.
Automation — the AI engine: incoming leads are captured, answered and followed up automatically (WhatsApp, missed-call follow-up), and the owner’s work is automated wherever it can be — so they need fewer hands, not more. The engine takes over; motion sustains itself.
Scaling — fuel and steering: paid campaigns, optimisation, reporting; and when more hands are genuinely needed, social recruiting to grow the team. Full speed, compounding growth.

What we need

Logo / wordmark for “Élan” (the É accent matters — it must work across French, German, Dutch and English, and as a favicon)
A standalone mark that lives on its own (app icon, avatar, pattern)
A symbol set — one mark per stage above, as a coherent family that reads as a forward-moving system, not four random icons
Color direction (see below)
A typography system, and specifically web brand guidelines: how headings, paragraphs and detail/caption text behave on screen — sizes, weights, hierarchy, spacing
Motion direction (movement is the core of “momentum” — a short note or a few frames, not full animation)
3–5 core applications: website hero, business card, social avatar, email signature
A concise, usable brand guide

Creative direction
Hold a tension: expressive and confident, but grounded. Our audience buys on trust, so we never tip into empty hype — but we’re not safe or boring either. We like identities that are outspoken and modern while still feeling nice, not aggressive. The boldness lives in motion, scale and a few dark, cinematic moments; the trust lives in warmth and restraint everywhere else.

On color: our palette leans toward the Luxembourg flag — red, a warm off-white, and a light sky-blue — as a quiet nod to where we’re rooted. Keep that direction; you don’t need to match the flag exactly, but the local reference should be felt. Full palette and type starting point are in the strategy doc we’ll share.

Our values (they should be felt in the work)
AI-first and modern, but privacy-respec

leads.title: SEO expert to review a site migration plan and redirect maps (two e-commerce sites, UK education)
leads.desc:
We’re a UK education publisher running two established e-commerce sites. One sells printable practice papers for school entrance exams and the other sells online practice tests for school entrance assessments. Both are on WordPress today. We’re rebuilding them on a single new platform, launching at the end of March 2027.

The planning is largely done, and what we need now is an experienced pair of eyes to check it before we build. For each site we have a new site structure and URL tree, a written brief explaining the decisions behind it, and a URL-by-URL redirect map. The larger map covers more than 1,300 editorial posts, with 16 months of Search Console data and linking domains against each one. The other covers more than 2,000 URLs, including around 1,500 products, with revenue for each product. Both maps already flag the high-risk URLs. The product and category redirect mapping for the larger site is still to do, and we’d welcome your input on it.

There are three parts to the work.

The first is a review and risk analysis of both plans. We’d like you to tell us where the structure, redirect rules or high-risk pages could cost us traffic or revenue, what we’ve missed, and what you’d change. The output should be a written report with each risk rated and a clear recommendation against it, plus comments directly in the redirect sheets where individual URLs need a different decision.

The second is a quick wins and 30-day plan for both sites as they stand today. That means an audit of organic opportunities scored on impact, effort and buyer intent, a prioritised list of pages to improve or create with the keywords and actions, and a technical cleanup list (duplicate URLs, legacy paths, canonicals) that we can carry straight into the migration.

The third is a controlled test. You’d pick a sample of high, medium and low risk pages and write a brief for each, applying the structural changes we’re planning for the new sites. Our developers make every change and handle any rollback, so you won’t touch the sites. You’d then monitor the test pages for 30 days and report back. The results will decide whether we launch everything at once or stagger the release, so we’d like them by mid-December.

We’d also like to hear how you would support the launch itself (staging checks, launch-day checks and aftercare), but please price that separately as an option.

On terms, this is a fixed-price contract, paid on delivering the work on time rather than on results. We don’t expect you to guarantee rankings or traffic. Your liability will be capped at the fee, and any change to the sites, and any dip from the test, is our decision and our risk. You’ll get Search Console and GA4 access for both sites. We’d like to start as soon as possible.

I am seeking an experienced medical or public health researcher to independently review and help finalize a clinical research project examining misinformation and knowledge gaps in public online discussions.

The study focuses on a particular post medical procedure lab test and the accuracy of medical advice shared in Reddit posts and comments, using applicable guidelines.

A preliminary research protocol, coding framework, and dataset have already been developed. The study uses a large language model (LLM) to assist with data screening and content classification.

I am looking for someone who can critically manually evaluate the methodology, identify potential errors, and help ensure the study is scientifically rigorous and ready for analysis. Prefer someone who has submitted scientific abstracts in the past to health relateed journals.

Responsibilities

Methodological review: Evaluate the study design, research question, inclusion/exclusion criteria, search strategy, and standardized codebook. Recommend corrections where necessary.

Independent coding validation: Independently review a pilot sample of approximately 25–40 original Reddit posts and comments, compare classifications against the LLM-assisted results, and document discrepancies.

Statistical analysis: Develop a reproducible analysis framework for misinformation prevalence, knowledge gaps, medical advice, corrective responses, and coding agreement. Address the statistical implications of multiple comments belonging to the same discussion thread.

Quality assurance: Identify missing data, inconsistent coding, potential selection bias, and unsupported clinical conclusions.

Expected deliverables

Written methodological audit and recommendations

Independent pilot coding and discrepancy spreadsheet

Statistical analysis plan with reproducible formulas or code

Specific recommendations for improving validity and reproducibility

Preferred qualifications

Graduate degree in epidemiology, public health, biostatistics, or a related field

Experience with medical research methodology and content analysis

Experience with inter-rater reliability and qualitative coding

Proficiency in R, Python, or Excel

Familiarity with clinical guidelines and AI-assisted research methods

Timeline: Urgent, with completion preferred within 3–5 days of starting.

Compensation: Fixed-price contract of $215, divided into milestones.

Please provide examples of similar research projects and briefly explain how you would independently validate an LLM-assisted content-analysis study.

I am specifically looking for someone who will identify methodological weaknesses and recommend improvements rather than simply confirm existing findings.

We need someone available to start promptly, identify the commercial and technical barriers to performance, and implement a clear recovery plan. There is potential for an ongoing relationship with the right person.

RELEVANT EXPERIENCE IS ESSENTIAL

We are particularly interested in candidates who have managed Google Ads for multi-brand sportswear, football/rugby merchandise, footwear, fashion or comparable retailers.

This account requires more than a standard Shopify campaign setup. You should understand the challenges of selling branded products that customers can also buy elsewhere, with demand and profitability varying significantly across products.

WHAT MAKES THIS ACCOUNT DIFFERENT

• Current-season kits, previous-season shirts, discounted stock, clothing and accessories require different commercial approaches.
• Size availability matters: a product can technically be in stock while having very few commercially useful sizes remaining.
• Demand varies by team, kit launch, fixtures, international tournaments and gifting periods.
• Customers searching for a team or country may want tickets, news or other sports rather than rugby merchandise.
• Sale products can generate stronger reported ROAS without necessarily generating the best profit.
• Conversion volume is limited enough that excessive campaign segmentation can be counterproductive.
• We need to distinguish brand demand from profitable acquisition of new customers.

Experience working through these issues is more valuable to us than experience managing large budgets alone.

THE OPPORTUNITY

The account has underperformed and campaigns are currently paused pending review. We need to establish a commercially viable foundation before scaling.

A media budget of up to approximately £10,000 per month is available initially, subject to performance. There is no requirement to spend it simply because it is available.

Our previous working target was approximately 4x ROAS. You will need to assess that against margins, VAT, discounts, returns and management costs, rather than assume that a headline ROAS figure guarantees profitability.

Upcoming trading periods and next year’s new ranges provide opportunities, but our immediate priority is proving that the account can acquire customers economically.

YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES

• Review Google Ads, Merchant Center, Shopify and conversion tracking.
• Validate purchase volumes and revenue against Shopify, investigating duplicate conversions, missing revenue and attribution differences.
• Review product feeds, variant IDs, titles, availability and useful product segmentation.
• Identify what is worth retaining, what should remain paused and what needs changing.
• Recommend an appropriately consolidated Shopping/PMax/Search structure based on available data.
• Control irrelevant traffic, campaign overl

leads.title: AI Developer to Build AI Agents / AI Agent Developer & Automation Engineer
leads.desc:
We are looking for an experienced AI Agent Developer and Automation Engineer to design, build and ship AI agents that automate real business work. You will take projects from idea to production, connect LLMs to our tools, APIs and data, and make sure the results are reliable, cost-aware and easy for our team to use.

The work covers:

Custom AI agents that use our tools and APIs to complete tasks on their own, with a person approving the important steps.
RAG chatbots that answer from our own documents and show the source behind each answer.
Workflow automation that connects CRMs, email, Slack, databases and other internal systems.
AI voice agents for calls and conversational support.
LLM integration (OpenAI, Anthropic and others) with sensible control over model costs, prompts and evaluation.
Python (FastAPI) backend services behind these features.
Simple React dashboards so our team can monitor and control the agents.

We expect fast delivery using AI coding tools such as Cursor and Claude Code.

Key Responsibilities

Design and develop autonomous agents, multi-step agent workflows and tool-calling pipelines.
Build RAG systems with vector databases, document ingestion, retrieval tuning and source citations.
Build and integrate backend services with Python (FastAPI) and Node.js.
Automate business processes using APIs, webhooks and tools such as n8n, Make or Zapier where they fit.
Add monitoring, logging, guardrails and human-in-the-loop approval steps to agent workflows.
Test and improve agent quality, speed and cost over time.
Write short updates and give a quick demo when each piece of work is done.

Required Skills & Expertise

Programming: Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Node.js
LLMs & Agents: OpenAI API, Anthropic API, function/tool calling, prompt engineering, LangChain, LangGraph or similar agent frameworks
RAG & Data: Vector databases (Pinecone, Qdrant, pgvector, etc.), embeddings, document processing, SQL
Automation & Integrations: REST APIs, webhooks, n8n/Make/Zapier, CRM and messaging integrations
Voice AI (a plus): Speech-to-text, text-to-speech, real-time voice agent platforms
Backend & Frontend: FastAPI, React, Docker, cloud deployment, Git
Nice to have: NLP, fine-tuning, machine learning, software architecture for scalable systems

What we need from you

Hands-on experience shipping LLM and agent features to real users, not just prototypes.
Comfort working inside an existing codebase.
Clear communication and the ability to work independently without hand-holding.

We will start with one first project and continue with more work after it.

leads.title: fixing META SHOPIFY event_source_url parameter issue
leads.desc:
Hello. I own an e-commerce store that was performing well in the Saudi market, but sales have suddenly dropped following the emergence of the following issue:
"Some events sent through Conversions API are blocked."
Conversions API:
Events sent via the Conversions API that lack the `event_source_url` parameter are being blocked because your business sends data from—or runs ads that link to—websites falling under restricted categories. (Learn more about these categories.)
You or your developer need to add the `event_source_url` parameter to the events sent through the Conversions API.
If you have the expertise to resolve this issue—or have encountered it before—please let me know so we can begin working together.

leads.title: [Short-term] Audio and Language Evaluator — Spanish (Argentina)
leads.desc:
Overview
We are seeking native-level Spanish (Argentina) speakers to support evaluation and annotation work for voice AI. Projects span text-to-speech audio evaluation, data annotation, transcript review, and linguistic analysis. You will assess outputs using structured rubrics and provide written feedback in English.

This is a short-term engagement lasting 1–3 months. 


About the Role
The work varies across projects. Some examples of what you may be asked to do:
- Listen to AI-generated audio samples in your language and rate them across multiple quality dimensions using a provided rubric.
- Compare pairs of audio samples and indicate which you prefer, along with how strong your preference is.
- Review and annotate transcripts for accuracy, segmentation, or linguistic features.
- Complete data annotation tasks that involve labeling, categorizing, or flagging content according to provided guidelines.
- Write short English-language feedback explaining your ratings, describing what you heard, and noting specific issues.

Rubrics cover quality dimensions such as accuracy of speech, rhythm, pitch, energy, and voice likeness, among others. Each task comes with specific instructions outlining what to assess and how to apply the rubric.

Each task includes evaluation guidelines and a rubric that define the required output. Contractors apply the rubric to produce ratings and written feedback that meet the specifications for each task and ensure ratings are aligned across the team. This means carefully reading the guidelines for each task, asking clarifying questions when something is unclear, and applying the same standards throughout your work. Tasks include reference examples so contractors can confirm their output meets the rubric specifications.


Volume
Contractors may work up to 20 hours per week, though actual volume depends on available tasks and may be limited in a given week.

We hold ad hoc team meetings, including meetings for your language group and important projects. Each task includes its own deadline, which is noted when the assignment is posted.

Typical turnaround for a task is 24 hours from assignment. Larger tasks will have extended deadlines.

Some tasks are planned in advance; others are ad hoc with shorter turnaround timelines.


Requirements
- Native-level proficiency in Spanish as spoken in Argentina.
- Strong written English proficiency. You will write feedback, read guidelines, and communicate with the team in English.
- Foundational knowledge of linguistics or a related field. You should be comfortable with concepts like phonetics, prosody, and intonation, and be able to apply them when evaluating speech. Formal education in linguistics, language studies, or speech science is a strong plus.
- Reliable internet connection, a computer with audio playback, and headphones.
- Ability to follow detailed guidelines precisely and maintain consistent quality across tasks.
- Join our Slack workspace and task platforms. Task assignmen

leads.title: SEO & Link Building Expert Needed to Increase Domain Rating (DR) for B2B SaaS Website

leads.title: Cold Email Campaign Specialist (Apollo/Clay, Separate Sending Domains) for AI SaaS
leads.desc:
We are Cysora, an AI SaaS that automates inbound sales conversations (WhatsApp, web chat, email) for businesses. We want to run outbound cold email to mid-market companies, but we must NOT put our main product domain's reputation at risk. Deliverability and spam score of our primary domain are non-negotiable.

WHAT WE NEED
Someone to design, build and run a cold email campaign for us, starting with a part-time first month, with the option to continue monthly based on results. We already send some cold email ourselves (30-50 per weekday) and want a specialist to do it properly, on separate domains, with better targeting and personalization.

TARGET
- Companies with 50-500 employees in sales-process-heavy industries (e.g. real estate, auto, education, healthcare/clinics, home services, financial services, B2B services)
- Decision makers: owners, heads of sales, marketing, operations

SCOPE (month 1)
1. Sending infrastructure: set up separate lookalike sending domains and mailboxes (not our main domain), with SPF, DKIM, DMARC, warm-up, and sensible daily caps. Tell us which tools you use and why.
2. Lead sourcing and list building in Apollo and/or Clay, with email verification and cleaning before anything is sent.
3. Personalization: pull each lead's website via Clay (or similar) and generate a short personalized opener per lead. We will generate a custom demo link per lead from their website; you merge that link into the email.
4. Copy: draft a 3-4 step sequence plus A/B variants, with our review before launch.
5. Launch and manage the campaign: send a minimum of 30-50 emails per weekday through the month, monitor bounces, spam complaints and reply rates, and hand positive replies to us.
6. Weekly written report: emails sent, delivered, bounce rate, reply rate, positive replies, demos booked, domain health, and what you will test next.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (what done looks like)
- Sending domains and mailboxes live, authenticated and warmed, documented in a short handover doc
- Verified, deduplicated leads matching our ICP, enough to keep sending 30-50 per weekday for the month
- Personalization workflow working end to end with the demo link merged per lead
- Campaign launched with our approval of copy
- Bounce rate under 3% and spam complaints under 0.1%
- Weekly report delivered every week, plus an end-of-month summary with recommendations
- We own the domains, lists and workflow accounts at handover

BUDGET AND HOURS
Hourly, with a weekly limit of roughly 5-10 hours (about $200 total for month 1). Tool and data costs (domains, mailboxes, sending tool, Apollo/Clay credits) are paid by us. If results are good, we continue monthly with more hours.

PLEASE IN YOUR PROPOSAL
Answer the screening questions, and share 1-2 past campaign examples (anonymized is fine) with results. Plain text answers please.

leads.title: [Short-term] Audio and Language Evaluator — Basque (Spain)
leads.desc:
Overview
We are seeking native-level Basque (Spain) speakers to support evaluation and annotation work for voice AI. Projects span text-to-speech audio evaluation, data annotation, transcript review, and linguistic analysis. You will assess outputs using structured rubrics and provide written feedback in English.

This is a short-term engagement lasting 3–4 weeks. 


About the Role
The work varies across projects. Some examples of what you may be asked to do:
- Listen to AI-generated audio samples in your language and rate them across multiple quality dimensions using a provided rubric.
- Compare pairs of audio samples and indicate which you prefer, along with how strong your preference is.
- Review and annotate transcripts for accuracy, segmentation, or linguistic features.
- Complete data annotation tasks that involve labeling, categorizing, or flagging content according to provided guidelines.
- Write short English-language feedback explaining your ratings, describing what you heard, and noting specific issues.

Rubrics cover quality dimensions such as accuracy of speech, rhythm, pitch, energy, and voice likeness, among others. Each task comes with specific instructions outlining what to assess and how to apply the rubric.

Each task includes evaluation guidelines and a rubric that define the required output. Contractors apply the rubric to produce ratings and written feedback that meet the specifications for each task and ensure ratings are aligned across the team. This means carefully reading the guidelines for each task, asking clarifying questions when something is unclear, and applying the same standards throughout your work. Tasks include reference examples so contractors can confirm their output meets the rubric specifications.


Volume
Contractors may work up to 20 hours per week, though actual volume depends on available tasks and may be limited in a given week.

We hold ad hoc team meetings, including meetings for your language group and important projects. Each task includes its own deadline, which is noted when the assignment is posted.

Typical turnaround for a task is 24 hours from assignment. Larger tasks will have extended deadlines.

Some tasks are planned in advance; others are ad hoc with shorter turnaround timelines.


Requirements
- Native-level proficiency in Basque as spoken in Spain.
- Strong written English proficiency. You will write feedback, read guidelines, and communicate with the team in English.
- Foundational knowledge of linguistics or a related field. You should be comfortable with concepts like phonetics, prosody, and intonation, and be able to apply them when evaluating speech. Formal education in linguistics, language studies, or speech science is a strong plus.
- Reliable internet connection, a computer with audio playback, and headphones.

Eligibility
The participating client must currently sustain at least 1,000 actual customer phone conversations per day. Bring an existing live client agent and compare it with Rasen on the same use case. Run 1,000 real production calls in total on Rasen, alongside the client's current setup. This 1,000-call evaluation target is separate from the 1,000-per-day eligibility minimum. No simulated or test-call top-ups.

- Platform experience: building, editing, debugging, deploying, API and documentation

Deliverables

We are targeting Friday, 23 October, subject to client permission, setup, approved traffic allocation and reporting effort. Please give realistic dates and estimated effort. Job title: Developer Needed to Build an Automated Website Vulnerability Scanner
I’m looking for an experienced developer or cybersecurity specialist to build a system where I can enter a website URL, run a security scan, and receive a clear report of potential vulnerabilities and recommended fixes.
This system is for ethical security testing of websites I own or have explicit permission to assess.
Tools to include
I want the system to use or integrate the following tools where appropriate:
- Burp Suite — web application security testing. Please explain your proposed automation approach and any licensing requirements.
- OWASP ZAP — automated website vulnerability scanning.
- Nuclei — template-based checks for known vulnerabilities, exposures, and misconfigurations.
- sqlmap — controlled SQL injection testing on approved targets, without extracting data or modifying databases.
- Gitleaks — detecting exposed secrets and credentials in repositories or source code I provide access to. This should be a separate feature alongside website scanning.
Please explain how you would combine these tools into one reliable system, including any integration limitations.
Main features
- A simple dashboard to enter a URL and launch a scan.
- Domain verification or an approved-target list.
- Configurable scan options, including which tools to run.
- Sensible rate limits, scan timeouts, and a stop button.
- Scan progress and previous scan history.
- One combined report that removes duplicate findings and flags results needing manual verification.
- Findings organised by severity, with affected URLs, supporting evidence, plain-English explanations, and recommended fixes.
- Downloadable PDF reports.
- Secure login and protected storage of scan results.
Deliverables
- A working system tested against authorised targets.
- Full source code and deployment instructions.
- Documentation covering setup, usage, maintenance, and scanning limitations.
- A handover session and an agreed period for fixing initial bugs.
Ideal experience
Experience building web applications, automating security tools, working with the tools listed above, and understanding OWASP web security risks.
Please include in your proposal
1. Examples of similar systems you have built.
2. Your recommended architecture and technology stack.
3. Which tools and features you would include in the first version.
4. Estimated cost and delivery timeline.
5. Any ongoing hosting, licensing, or API costs.
6. Your approach to reducing false positives and avoiding disruption during scans.
My priority is a practical, reliable first version that is easy to use and can be expanded later.

The website will serve residential customers and commercial buyers, including architects, designers, builders, contractors, installers, dealers, restaurants, hotels, and more.

We are seeking **senior full-stack WordPress/WooCommerce developers and a technical lead** to take ownership of the platform’s technical architecture, implementation, integrations, quality, and maintainability.

leads.title: Senior Healthcare SaaS Development Developer
leads.desc:
Senior Healthcare SaaS Development Team Needed — EHR/EMR, Home Health, Behavioral Health, EVV, Billing, Telehealth & AI

We are seeking an experienced healthcare software architect or development team to design and build a proprietary healthcare SaaS platform called Foundations HealthOS. This is not a basic website, CRM, or scheduling application.

We are developing an integrated healthcare operations platform combining functionality found across behavioral-health EHR systems, home-health EMRs, practice-management systems, EVV platforms, telehealth systems, revenue-cycle platforms, workforce-management systems, and AI-assisted clinical documentation tools.

The platform will initially be used internally by Foundations Senior Services and should be architected for potential future commercialization as a multi-tenant SaaS product.
Core Workflow
The system must support an end-to-end workflow:

Referral → AI Intake → Eligibility → Authorization → Admission → Scheduling → Visit/Telehealth → EVV → Clinical Documentation → QA → Billing → Claims → Payment → Denials/Appeals → Reporting

Our goal is:

One Patient. One Record. One Workflow.
Critical Requirement: AI-Powered Referral Intake
This is one of the most important components of the project.

Referrals may enter the system through:
- Integrated document transmission
- Referral portal
- Online referral forms
- Secure document upload
- Authorized electronic integrations
- API/interface
- Manual document upload
When a referral is received, the platform should use OCR and document AI to read, classify, and process the referral package and automatically populate the patient intake record. Staff should not have to manually re-enter information already contained in the referral.

The AI should extract available information including:
- Patient demographics
- Date of birth
- Address
- Contact information
- Insurance
- Member ID
- Medicaid/Medicare information
- VA/TriWest referral information
- Authorization numbers
- Authorization dates
- Approved visits or units
- CPT/HCPCS codes
- ICD-10 diagnoses
- Physicians
- Physician identifiers
- Medications
- Allergies
- Requested services
- Service frequency
- Clinical history
- Other structured information
The system must support:
- Document classification
- Multi-page referral packages
- Document splitting
- Duplicate-patient detection
- Existing-patient matching
- Confidence scoring
- Missing-data detection
- Conflicting-data detection
- Source-document tracking
- Human verification before uncertain information becomes final
The desired workflow is:

Referral Received → AI Reads Documents → Patient Match → Intake Auto-Populated → Insurance Created → Authorization Created → Physician/Referral Source Linked → Staff Reviews Exceptions → Approve & Create Client
Integrated Healthcare Document Transmission
We need secure inbound and outbound healthcare document transmission built into the platform through an established compliant API provider.

We’re looking for a marketing manager who can work across our tools, channels, and team—and do the work, not just delegate it.

You do need the confidence to learn, the judgment to test your changes, and the sense to ask for help before a small fix becomes a bigger problem.

Get hands-on with the tools. Make routine updates yourself, check the result, and bring in specialists when the work needs deeper expertise.

Keep the customer journey connected. Check what happens between an ad or social post, a landing page, a form, a CRM record, and a follow-up email. Find where people get lost and help fix it.
Keep records and email useful. Maintain clear CRM data, lists, segments, and follow-up flows. Work with existing owners rather than creating parallel systems.

Make measurement trustworthy. Check links, tracking, and reports. Separate what the data shows from what we still need to verify. Turn findings into a clear next action.

Protect the brand. Catch generic AI copy, inconsistent messaging, broken links, and unsupported claims before they reach someone’s screen.

Work with outside partners. Give useful briefs, review deliverables, and follow through on fixes. You should be able to ask good technical questions—not just forward messages between people.

The stack you’ll work across includes:
Shopify: website and landing-page work (may transition to Webflow)

Zoho: CRM records, partner information, and follow-up tracking.

Klaviyo: email campaigns, lists, and automated flows (may transition to Beehiiv)

Funraise and RingCentral: additional platforms you’ll need to learn and work across as responsibilities are agreed.

Google and Meta advertising tools: campaign coordination and checks with our paid-media partners, subject to approved plans and budgets.

You should also be comfortable with web analytics and diagnosing tracking gaps. Some access, reporting, and connections still need work. Part of your value is knowing what needs to be checked before anyone trusts the numbers.

What we’re looking for
Hands-on marketing experience across web, email, CRM, paid social or search, and reporting. You’ve shipped work—not only presented plans.

leads.title: Gated Login for Shopify Store
leads.desc:
Shopify Wholesale Store – Customer Approval & Secure Login

We have a separate Shopify wholesale store on the Basic plan. We need a developer to set up secure customer registration, manual approval, and login restrictions.

CURRENT PROBLEM:

Anyone can enter their email, receive a Shopify verification code, and access our wholesale store without approval. We must prevent this.

WHAT WE NEED:
1. New customers complete our existing Shopify Forms application with their business details.
2. We manually approve or reject each application.
3. Unapproved customers cannot access wholesale prices or place orders.
4. Approved customers can log in, view prices, and purchase normally.
5. Ideally, visitors can browse products without seeing wholesale prices.
6. Security must be enforced at checkout, not just by hiding prices or buttons.
OUR CURRENT SETUP:
- Shopify Basic plan
- Shopify B2B enabled with an active B2B market
- Wholesale application already created using Shopify Forms
REQUIREMENTS:

We prefer native Shopify features or lightweight apps. No complicated custom system or website redesign.

PLEASE TELL US:
- How you would implement this on Shopify Basic.
- Whether paid apps are needed and their monthly costs.
- Your experience with similar wholesale stores.
MOST IMPORTANT: The system must be secure, simple, and reliable. Retail customers must never be able to bypass approval and purchase at wholesale prices.

Here’s the problem. We get the lead to the door, and then a lot of it falls apart. Calls go unanswered, follow-up is slow or doesn’t happen, nobody asks for reviews, and old customers never hear from the business again. We want to fix what happens after the lead, inside HighLevel, for our existing clients.

Capture: get every lead into a CRM pipeline. Forms and landing pages connected to workflows, plus a Voice AI agent that answers every call, 24/7, logs the details, and hands off to a person when it should.

leads.title: Machine Learning Engineer — One Seat on a Small Team That Gets Sent In
leads.desc:
Every large company has a standing army of engineers: thousands of people, each owning one narrow slice, moving at the speed of the slowest approval.

This is the other thing. The small team that gets sent in when the standing army can’t solve it.

We’re a small, senior engineering unit with a standing mandate across a growing family of companies in a range of industries. When one of them hits a problem its own people can’t crack (a process drowning in manual work, a model nobody trusts, a question of whether machine learning belongs there at all), we get sent in. There are more problems waiting than people to send. That’s why this seat is open.

We add one person at a time, and we take our time choosing. We’d rather leave a seat empty than fill it wrong. One seat is open now, for a machine learning engineer.

THE WORK
You’ll be dropped into a company you’ve never seen. The data will be uncleaned, the process half-documented, and the people who’ve done the job by hand for years will know things that aren’t written down anywhere. Your assignment arrives as an objective, not a spec:

“This workflow runs on manual classification. Find out whether we can automate it, and prove it.”
“The model they’re using gives inconsistent answers. Find out why. Tell us what to change.”
“Someone thinks there’s an ML opportunity in this process. Find out whether they’re right.”

You learn the terrain fast. You interrogate the data and sit with the operators. You set a baseline and define what “good” means before you build anything. Then you choose the tool: an LLM, gradient boosting, a retrieval system, or 200 lines of deterministic code. And you’ll have the standing to say “don’t build this” when that’s the right answer.

What you ship has to keep working after we’ve moved on. Tests, monitoring, rollback, documentation. A business will be running on it.

IT WILL BE HARD
The data will be worse than you expect. Requirements will shift after you’ve started. You’ll spend three weeks on an approach, learn it’s wrong, and the right move will be to throw it out without flinching. The person you most need to talk to will be too busy. And you’ll be judged on whether the thing works, not on how hard you tried.

If that paragraph made you lean in rather than back, keep reading.

WHY THIS AND NOT THE BIG-COMPANY JOB
At a large company you own a metric. Your model is one of four hundred. You’ll spend a quarter in launch review, never meet the person whose job your work changed, and watch your best idea die in a planning doc.

Here, you are the machine learning capability. What you decide is what gets built. You’ll see more real ML problems in two years than most engineers see in ten: different industries, different data, different ways things break. You’ll learn how businesses actually make money, from inside them, alongside the people who own them and make the calls. And your work will go into production at companies that run on it. The people who run them will know your name.

leads.title: AI Quality Manager / QA Lead for AI-First Insurance Product (German C1+ required)

QA for AI products is a discipline that barely exists yet. We run up to thousands of automated tests per day plus continuous manual testing by a pool of freelance testers. You own the why: what we test, why, to what depth, and how the testing operation is organized. You define what a "correct" answer is. A well-written answer is still wrong if it contradicts the insurance policy. Business and user-value thinking matters more than deep technical knowledge.

What you will do
- Own the AI testing strategy: what gets tested, why, and to what depth
- Define what "correct" means for our AI answers and turn it into clear evaluation criteria
- Organize test sets across many parallel variations (often 50 at once)
- Review and mark AI outputs, and define how manual testers evaluate them

- AI-native: you work with tools like Claude Code every day and understand how LLM products behave and fail
- Startup experience

- Strong self-organization across parallel tracks and constant change

Big pluses
- **Insurance background** (e.g. claims, underwriting, policy wording, customer service or product at an insurer, broker or insurtech). You will judge whether AI answers about insurance policies are correct, so domain knowledge counts a lot
- You have built or run an AI evaluation setup yourself (golden answer sets, LLM-as-judge, regression testing)

Full-time (40 h/week), long-term, CET working hours. We start with a short paid trial so both sides can check the fit.

- Which model for which job, and when to route a request to a different one.
- How a preset like "dolly-in" or "VHS look" turns into prompts and parameters that give consistent results across models.

Stack (fixed): Next.js App Router + TypeScript + Tailwind, PostgreSQL self-hosted in Docker Compose on a Hetzner VPS (Caddy, GitHub Actions deploy), AWS S3 + CloudFront, fal.ai for every model, Stripe (subscriptions + credit packs), Auth.js, next-intl, Resend, Sentry.

A damage claim is submitted through Microsoft Forms.

We collect the required documents and check whether the case file is complete.

Once complete, we transfer the claim to the relevant insurer or claims handler and notify the form submitter.

We track acknowledgements, follow-ups and settlement progress.

When the claim is closed, we send a final notification and complete the administrative record.

The form submitter and the affected customer may be different people. One customer may also have multiple claims. Contacts, cases, documents and communications must therefore be correctly linked.

Scope of work

1. Automated intake and case creation

Automatically create a claim record with a unique reference.

Create or update associated contacts without unnecessary duplicates.

Map form responses to the correct HubSpot properties.

Assign a case owner and create initial tasks.

Automatically create and link a case folder where needed.

Support different insurers and claims handlers.

Our existing Excel tracker contains insurer details, claim references, incident dates, customer contact information, investigation status, document request and receipt dates, reminders, insurer acknowledgements, handover and closure dates, communication milestones, compensation, financial administration, notes and time spent.

Research each hotel on my existing spreadsheet, one by one.

Find the hotel's official WhatsApp number rather than simply providing its office telephone number.

Check the hotel's official website, official Instagram or Facebook page, Google Maps listing, and other reliable sources.

Verify that the number is explicitly listed or linked as a WhatsApp contact wherever possible. Or is it a scam number, I will tell you more about this later.

Strong web research and data entry skills.

Excellent attention to detail.

Comfortable using Google Sheets or Microsoft Excel.

Able to communicate clearly in English. Knowledge of Bahasa Indonesia is a strong advantage.

For verification status, use:

Verified: WhatsApp number is explicitly published by an official hotel source.

Cross-Checked: Number is supported by credible sources but its WhatsApp use or official ownership is not fully confirmed.

Not Found: No reliable WhatsApp number could be identified.

Accuracy is more important than speed. Please do not guess numbers or submit ordinary office phone numbers as WhatsApp contacts.

What sources would you use to find official hotel WhatsApp numbers in Indonesia?

leads.title: Software architect with hands on Mastra.ai experience
leads.desc:
Looking for an architect/consultant with hands-on Mastra experience to help design an AI assistant embedded in a CRM and booking system.

Stack: Next.js, Supabase/Postgres, Railway.

The assistant should behave like a junior administrator across an ongoing customer/booking lifecycle:

Work across emails, internal notes, call transcripts, documents and current CRM records.
Investigate a situation using tools, then prepare related updates, draft replies, documents and follow-ups for human review.
Handle multiple email conversations about the same booking, with different participants and topics.
Stay aware of changes made directly by staff or customers in the application.
Continue unfinished work across later messages, approvals and long histories.
Email is one channel. Staff might also leave an internal instruction, mention the assistant in a note, or change a booking status.

Example: A customer requests a discount by email. A manager approves it in an internal note. The assistant should connect that decision to the original request, check the current booking and pricing, and prepare the appropriate updates and customer reply. Meanwhile, another conversation concerns booking details. If those details change before someone approves the draft, the assistant needs to account for that.

We’d like help choosing a practical architecture for:

Thread/session boundaries and shared customer/booking context.
Current application state versus conversation memory and retrieved evidence.
Wake-up rules, batching routine edits and continuing pending work.
Human approval, retries and avoiding duplicate actions.
Which Mastra facilities to use and what should remain application code.
The aim is a maintainable implementation with as few moving parts as reasonably possible.

leads.title: Python + ffmpeg tool: cut a long video into captioned vertical Shorts
leads.desc:
We make YouTube videos with an automated pipeline (Python, ffmpeg, AI voice and avatar tools). We need one more step built as a small standalone command line tool. This is a small fixed price job, paid through Upwork. Please don't start the work or send samples before you're hired. We pay for everything you build.

WHAT THE TOOL DOES

Inputs:
1. A long 16:9 MP4, 10 to 60 minutes.
2. A JSON file listing the clips to cut. Each clip has a name, a start time and an end time, for example: name clip01, start 00:01:05.200, end 00:01:48.000.
3. Optional: an SRT captions file for the whole long video.

For each clip it writes:
1. A 1080x1920 MP4 (H.264 video, AAC audio) at the source frame rate, with frame accurate cuts.
2. Framing set by an option: "crop" (center crop, with an optional left or right offset) or "fill" (the whole 16:9 frame in the middle, with a blurred, enlarged copy of it behind).
3. If an SRT was given: the captions for that clip's time range, retimed to the clip and burned in. White text with a black outline in the lower third. Font file, size and position set by options. A caption line that crosses the clip's start or end is trimmed to fit, not dropped.
4. Audio normalized to an integrated loudness of minus 14 LUFS.
5. A JPG contact sheet of 6 evenly spaced frames, so we can check the clip at a glance.

REQUIREMENTS
1. Runs on macOS (Apple Silicon) with Python 3.11 or newer and ffmpeg from Homebrew. No paid services, no cloud, no GPU.
2. One command runs everything. Each setting above can be changed with a command line option.
3. Clear error messages when a file is missing or a clip's times fall outside the video. One bad clip shouldn't stop the others.
4. A README with install steps, one example run and every option explained.
5. Test it on any Creative Commons video, for example Blender's open movie Big Buck Bunny. We'll also test it on our own footage.
6. AI coding tools are fine. You're responsible for the code working.

NOT INCLUDED: transcription (we already have captions), face tracking, uploading.

DONE WHEN: we run your example command on our Mac and on one of our own videos, and every clip comes out at the right size and length, with the captions in sync and no manual fixes. One round of fixes is included.

TIMELINE: please deliver within 5 days of being hired.

PAYMENT: one fixed price milestone, funded when you're hired and released when the test above passes. We review within 2 business days of delivery.

If this goes well we may have more pipeline work, but we can't promise it.

leads.title: Multi-Tenant Voice AI Receptionist Engine
leads.desc:
Project Goal
To build a scalable, low-latency, multi-tenant Voice AI receptionist system tailored for local home-service businesses (starting with plumbers). The architecture must completely bypass premium orchestration wrappers (like Vapi/Retell) to achieve a target operating cost of $0.03 to $0.04 USD per minute using an open-source pipeline.
2. Required Core Architecture
You are required to build and stitch the pipeline using the following open-source and wholesale infrastructure components:
• Telephony Carrier: Telnyx (preferred for lower latency) or Twilio.
• Orchestration Framework: LiveKit Agents (Python or TypeScript) or Pipecat.
• Speech-to-Text (STT): Deepgram Nova-2 via streaming WebSockets.
• Large Language Model (LLM): OpenAI GPT-4o-mini or Groq Llama-3.1-70B.
• Text-to-Speech (TTS): Cartesia (Sonic) or Deepgram Aura.
3. Key Feature Requirements
• Dynamic Multi-Tenancy: The backend engine must handle calls for multiple independent plumbing businesses simultaneously. When a call hits the telephony webhook, the system must read the incoming dialed number (to_number), look it up in a central database, and dynamically inject that specific business's Company Name, Operating Rules, and Instruction Prompt into the LLM context.
• Conversational Logic: The AI must politely greet callers, collect their name, phone number, and a description of their plumbing issue. If an active flood/emergency is mentioned, it must provide immediate safety instructions (e.g., “Please turn off your main water valve immediately while I notify our technician”).
• End-of-Call Webhook (Data Routing): Within 30 seconds of a call hanging up, the system must trigger an outbound JSON payload/webhook containing the full call transcript, an AI-generated 2-sentence summary, and the extracted customer contact details.
4. Out of Scope (What you do NOT need to build)
• You do not need to build a custom frontend user dashboard for clients.
• You do not need to build complex custom text-messaging features; we will be using a simple webhook connected to Make.com to handle the post-call routing to Google Sheets and SMS.
5. Hosting & Deployment
• The final production-ready code repository must be securely deployed onto a scalable, low-cost cloud provider (Railway, DigitalOcean, or AWS) using a Docker container or equivalent configuration.
• All environment variables must point to API accounts owned and funded by me.

Next Steps to Send with This:

Ask your candidate: "Please review this specification sheet. If you agree to these exact technical terms and the milestone schedule we discussed, please send me an official Upwork offer for this project so we can fund Milestone 1 and begin work today."
While they review this spec sheet, would you like me to map out the exact columns and sample data for your Airtable/Google Sheets database so you can hand it straight to them on Day 1?

We need an experienced engineer to guide the direction, design the approach, and review key milestones for our AI agent project. The work includes planning the program, improving data extraction, and helping build a knowledge base to support the system. You will help ensure the solution is well-structured, efficient, and aligned with our goals from the start.

We are two consultancies building a free AI agent that helps nonprofits plan their programs and how they will measure them. It walks users through a three-step planning framework: a theory of change, a logic model, and a logframe (the results table that lists goals, outputs, outcomes, indicators, and assumptions). The pilot focuses on family planning, a field with well-established global indicators and strong professional networks for sourcing and testing. 

The questions we need help with
1.	Extraction from PDFs. What is the best way to use AI to pull usable content out of messy PDFs? Logframes are usually multi-page tables, theories of change are often diagrams, some files are scanned, and terminology varies a lot between organizations. We want a process our analysts can run and repeat.
2.	Whole documents vs. extracted pieces. Our current leaning is to keep whole documents with rich tags, because breaking them apart can lose the logic linking one level to the next. We also need structured data, such as each outcome and the indicators that measure it. How should we balance the two?
3.	Data structure. How should we represent the results chain (impact → outcome → output → activity → indicator) and our tags so the data works for the agent? What should our metadata and rules files look like?
4.	Vector database. We plan to use a vector database (one that lets the agent search by meaning, not just exact words). We need advice on which one, how to structure it, and hands-on help setting it up.
5.	Models, hosting, and cost. Our preference is to build on an existing commercial AI model rather than train our own, likely hosted in Microsoft Azure. We want a sanity check on that and a rough estimate of running costs.

- Play the game often and give the agent specific feedback. “Jumping feels floaty because gravity is too low” is useful. “Make it better” is not.
- Keep going until the game compiles, runs and is fun to play.
- Write up a few of the hard technical problems you hit, using a template and tools we provide, then package and submit the game.

The back-and-forth is what matters most to us: what you notice, how you diagnose it, and how you push the agent toward a fix.

Pay

$100 per approved, completed game. Once you’re set up, each game should take no more than a couple of hours to create, and you’ll be able to build several in parallel while the coding agents are running. We can make 1 game for $100 or up to 5 for $500. We may have further contracts in future.

- Hands-on Unreal Engine experience (Blueprints and/or C++), professional or serious hobby.

Clear written communication and the ability to follow a detailed setup guide.

Requirements

- Unreal Engine 5.7, installed through the Epic Games Launcher.

- A paid Claude Code or Codex plan.
- GitHub and Epic Games accounts.
- A stable internet connection that can handle large uploads.

How your work is used

We’re studying how experienced developers build games with AI coding agents, so the build process matters more to us than the finished game. Your direction to the agent, the problems you hit and how you solved them are used to help improve AI coding tools. We don’t release the games as products.

Our tools only log what happens inside your game sessions, and they record in plain text, so you can see exactly what’s captured at any time. We’ll guide you through setup and do a short kickoff call before your first game.

leads.title: Paid Ads and Conversion Tracking Audit for Kaedrin
leads.desc:
We’re looking for an advertising specialist to review a small set of existing Kaedrin campaigns and help us understand our spending, conversion tracking and next practical improvement.

Kaedrin provides resume and career document services. We use Google Ads, Meta Ads and ChatGPT Ads. This assignment is a focused diagnostic, with the campaigns and reporting period agreed before work begins.

What we need
1. Spending and activity review
Compare reported spending, configured budgets and campaign activity using the records provided. Distinguish advertising spend from billed charges and flag discrepancies or missing information.
2. Conversion tracking diagnosis
Review how clicks connect to genuine inquiries, qualified buyers and payments. Identify where measurement breaks down and recommend the smallest practical fix using our existing systems.
3. One prioritized improvement
Recommend one bounded test. Explain why it deserves priority, its estimated cost, how success would be measured and when we should stop. If the evidence does not justify a campaign test, explain which information or measurement must be established first.
4. Knowledge transfer
Deliver a short written report with supporting evidence, diagnostic steps and reusable instructions. Clearly separate verified findings from assumptions and unanswered questions. We want practical guidance we can understand and use, not a slide deck. You should be comfortable working independently, following written instructions and documenting your reasoning so our team can reuse what you learn.

Scope and access
This is a review only. No ad changes, budget increases, campaign launches, tracking implementation or ongoing management are included.
We will initially provide reports and appropriately redacted exports. Any additional access must be agreed separately. We will not share passwords. Use aggregate purchase information or redacted transaction evidence only. No customer names, resumes, payment credentials or unrestricted customer records.
We understand that incomplete data may prevent a definitive diagnosis. Explain those limits rather than guessing. This engagement does not guarantee further work.

Relevant experience
Please have hands on Google Ads and Meta Ads measurement experience. ChatGPT Ads familiarity is helpful, but be honest about your experience with each platform.

Please answer these questions
1. Describe a case where you investigated a mismatch between reported conversions and actual revenue. What did you find?
2. What would you check first for this assignment?
3. Which advertising platforms and tracking tools have you personally used?
Please confirm that you can complete this bounded review for $150 and state your expected turnaround time.
